carried_rule: Of L's three seeds (segL-s1, -s2, -s3; plan training.seeds), the carried model is the one whose validation gap recovered in range (tma2-segment --segmenter L then tma2-gs, seed 314 scoring ordinals 500-1499, the plan's parameters, mode gap) is the median of the three; ties to the lower seed. Its best.safetensors is frozen by SHA-256 in an amendment before the test split is opened.
criterion: All on every sigma = 1 deg G5 row (zig + 5/10/15/20 min where reached) of the seed-315 test split (10,000 scenarios), with scenario-clustered paired bootstraps, 2,000 resamples, 97.5%. Gap recovered = (median one-leg error - median segmentation error) / (median one-leg error - median oracle error), raw relative range error (no CRB normalisation), tma2-gs's median convention (inverted_cdf). S1 (sanity): O's contamination P90 over ownship-leg prefixes at or below 0.02, point and upper bound. S2: C minus GLR + confirm, gap recovered in range: pass if the point and the whole interval lie above zero; fail if the whole interval lies at or below zero; otherwise inconclusive. S3: L minus the reference in contamination median and in contamination P90: point and upper bound at or below +0.01 each; L minus the reference in false-split rate (prefixes on scenarios with no target change): point and upper bound at or below +0.05. A difference, not an absolute rate, because C itself is at 0.083 on validation (2 of 24 change-free prefixes); pass if all hold, fail if any lower bound exceeds its limit, otherwise inconclusive. S4 (the only learning claim): L minus the reference, gap recovered in range: pass, fail and inconclusive as for S2, subject to the shuffled rule. Inconclusive counts as not passed for the follow-on.
follow_on: Annex A section A.9 and spec 005 FR-072: if S4 passes, L is Gate 2's segmenter and its control. Otherwise the reference (C, or GLR + confirm if S2 fails) carries into Gate 2 and learning is recorded as not shown. In either case Gate 2 reports its 'half the gap to the oracle' for the carried classical segmenter too, so a Gate 2 gain is attributed correctly.
forecast: S1 pass (O's contamination is 0 on every validation ownship leg). S2 pass, C minus GLR + confirm about +0.6 [+0.5, +0.7] in gap recovered (validation +0.63). S3 pass, L's contamination within 0.01 of C's (P90 near 0.27) and false splits unchanged, because the evidence's shift of the confirmation threshold is capped at tau/2. S4: C already recovers 0.89 of the gap, leaving 0.11. Forecast L minus C +0.01 [-0.01, +0.03], most likely inconclusive; probability of a pass about 30%.
s2_validation: Seed 314, scoring ordinals 500-1499, 3,934 G5 rows (experiments/20261104-gs-val/c-final): C (gap) minus GLR + confirm, gap recovered in range, +0.632 [0.558, 0.734] (97.5%, scenario-clustered, 2,000 resamples); course +0.49, speed +0.56, intervals above zero. Implied S4 reference: C. On test, S2 is decided again; if it does not pass, the reference for S3 and S4 is whichever of C and GLR + confirm has the higher test gap recovered in range.
shuffled_rule: The shuffled-label control (segL-shuffled: each training scenario's truth codes replaced by another's) is scored as the seeds are. Its validation gap recovered in range minus C's, paired and clustered at 97.5%, must have an interval that includes zero or lies below it. If the interval lies above zero, evidence trained without true labels beats C, so a gain by L cannot be attributed to learning: S4 is then recorded as not passed whatever its test interval, and the follow-on for a failed S4 applies.
